sentence: The theory predicts what the corpus shows: a generic technology yields nothing defensible by itself, because rivals can buy and deploy the same thing
passage: [Kemp (2024), p. 620] "For example, AI's generic nature is akin to general human capital. General human capital cannot typically underly interfirm advantages because a firm's competitors can usually acquire and deploy that knowledge in ways that closely mimic corresponding actions of the focal firm."

gemini.note: The passage offers a theoretical premise about the nature of generic technology, but the sentence presents this as an empirical finding from a corpus.
